waterbody.name: Rio Baco (historical name; Baco River candidate)
waterbody.identityBasis: The 1908 source names Camp Balete, Rio Baco, Mindoro. This is a textual historical locality link; no modern reach, river geometry, or station crosswalk was reviewed.

question: Which fish names does the 1908 primary paper explicitly associate with Camp Balete, Rio Baco, and can those names be normalized without overstating specimen provenance?

sourceReview.source: Jordan, D. S., & Richardson, R. E. (1908). Fishes from islands of the Philippine Archipelago. Bulletin of the Bureau of Fisheries, 27 (for 1907), 233–287. Bureau of Fisheries Document No. 640.
sourceReview.accessMethod: Read the NOAA-hosted paper text at printed pp. 241, 255, 258, and 274; no bulk download or contact was made.
sourceReview.collectionContext: The introduction says Richard C. McGregor brought a collection made in outlying Philippine islands to Stanford in 1906. The paper does not assign a collection date to each Rio Baco specimen, so no specimen event year is inferred.
sourceReview.localityCaveat: Camp Balete / Rio Baco is preserved verbatim. No modern coordinates, boundary, named reach, or municipality-level crosswalk was added. The 'above tide' qualifier appears for three of the four source entries only and is not transferred to Barbodes hemictenus.

records.localityVerbatim: One specimen was taken at Camp Balete, Rio Baco, Mindoro.
records.taxonomicCrosswalk: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes lists Barbodes hemictenus as valid.
records.voucherLinkage: The paper lists type CAS-SU 20213 and cotypes USNM 61685 for the species, but does not identify which cataloged specimen was taken at Camp Balete. Do not attach either catalog number to the Rio Baco specimen.
records.disposition: Retain as a historical species-level Rio Baco occurrence candidate; no exact Baco voucher, collection date, or mapped reach is resolved.

records.localityVerbatim: One of the smaller Mindoro specimens was taken from the Rio Baco, above tide, at Camp Balete.
records.taxonomicCrosswalk: GBIF Backbone accepts the species-rank name Kuhlia marginata.
records.voucherLinkage: No catalog number for the Camp Balete specimen is given in this passage.
records.disposition: Retain as a historical source-reported occurrence candidate, not a present-day or mapped-reach assertion.

records.localityVerbatim: A specimen, 5 inches long, from Camp Balete, Rio Baco, Mindoro, above tide.
records.taxonomicCrosswalk: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes lists Lutjanus argentimaculatus as valid; the historical genus spelling is normalized to Lutjanus.
records.voucherLinkage: No catalog number for the Camp Balete specimen is given in this passage.
records.disposition: Retain as a historical source-reported occurrence candidate, not a present-day or mapped-reach assertion.

records.localityVerbatim: A large male, 8.50 inches long, from Camp Balete, Rio Baco, Mindoro (above tide).
records.taxonomicCrosswalk: Held. The current-name crosswalk remains unresolved across the reviewed taxonomy sources; do not count this as a normalized species record until the name concept is reconciled.
records.voucherLinkage: No catalog number for the Camp Balete specimen is given in this passage.
records.disposition: Preserve the verbatim historical name as a held candidate only; exclude from the accepted-name count and app data.

interpretation.result: The primary paper explicitly associates three currently resolvable species names with Camp Balete, Rio Baco: Barbodes hemictenus, Kuhlia marginata, and Lutjanus argentimaculatus. It also reports Ophiocara aporos there, but that name remains held pending taxonomic reconciliation.
interpretation.historicalScope: These are historical source-reported records from a paper published in 1908. The collection context mentions 1906, but the source does not tie an exact collection date to each Baco specimen.
interpretation.specimenScope: The species account for Barbodes hemictenus lists type/cotype identifiers but does not connect one to the Camp Balete individual. The other Rio Baco entries lack catalog identifiers in the cited passages.
interpretation.candidateDisposition: Useful as a historical inland-water evidence lead. Keep all entries research-only until current taxonomy, exact voucher provenance, collection dates, and modern locality resolution are assessed.

limitations: A historical place-name mention does not resolve the modern river reach, municipal boundary, or precise specimen coordinates.
The Baco-locality individuals are not individually crosswalked to catalog numbers in the passages reviewed.
The 1906 date describes the broader collection context and is not an event date for each Rio Baco specimen.
Ophiocara aporos is retained verbatim but not normalized because its current taxonomic concept is unresolved in the reviewed crosswalk work.
Historical occurrence does not establish present-day occurrence, abundance, catchability, diet, legal access, fishing rules, water quality, or safety.
Reuse terms for the NOAA-hosted scan were not independently established; no scan pages, figures, or extended text were copied into this artifact.

followUp.nextAction: A follow-up cross-check found Kottelat's explicitly tentative '[possibly Camp Balete, Rio Baco ?]' type-locality note for CAS-SU 20213; see mimaropa-baco-hemictenus-type-locality-crosscheck-20261106.json. The original Baco individual is still not linked to a catalog number or event date. Continue the separate MIMAROPA freshwater source sweep; do not convert these historical candidates into current presence or fishing advice.
